This appellant has been convicted under Sections 363 of IPC to undergo RI for three years and fine of Rs.100/-, under Section 366-A of IPC to undergo RI for seven years and fine of Rs.200/-, under Section 376 (2) (n) of IPC to undergo RI for ten years and fine of Rs.500/-, under Section 5 (i)/6 of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act to undergo RI for ten years and fine of Rs.500/-

sentences.text:
On a specific query from the bench, Shri Rajput fairly admitted that the victim has already solemnized marriage with some other person, and residing with him.
In the aforesaid factual backdrop, without expressing any conclusive opinion on merits of the case,
we deem it proper to suspend the remaining jail sentence of the appellant.
Accordingly, I.A. No.5225 of 2023 is allowed.
Subject to depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited), the remaining jail sentence of appellant - Kamlesh is hereby suspended and it is directed that appellant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond for a sum of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Thirty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court with a further direction to appear before the trial Court, Harda on 4th September 2023 and also on such other dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard during the pendency of this appeal.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
First application was dismissed as withdrawn by order dated 25.6.2024 passed in MCRC No. 10084 of 2024 with liberty to repeat prayer for bail after examination of prosecutrix.
As per prosecution story, prosecutrix was going with her husband on tamtam when the offence was committed by two unknown persons whereas, as per court-statement, she was travelling in a Marshal car with her husband who called two persons on phone who committed rape upon her.
Even though prosecutrix is a major lady having knowledge about legal procedures, FIR has been lodged after a delay of 14 days on 19.2.2024 for which no plausible explanation has been given.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel for the applicant / accused argued that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
It is further argued that Kamlesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82437304/
1 applicant is in custody since 21.2.2024.
Further custodial interrogation of the applicant is not required.
Further argument is that applicant is the permanent resident of District - Morena (M.P.)
having no criminal antecedents.
On the other hand, learned State counsel vehemently opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.
opennyai_summary.final__ANALYSIS:
After withdrawal of first bail application, prosecutrix as well as her mother have been examined before the trial Court, however, there are material contradictions and omissions in her statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr..C. with her court-statement.
Since evidence of the prosecutrix has already been recorded,
therefore, question of influencing her does not arise.
